correctness.rationale: For a fixed source the common profile cancels, so the number of resulting profiles is the number of distinct changes. If a=b or b=c an internal change is −e_bb; otherwise the added coordinate e_ac cannot coincide with a removed coordinate, and the two removed ordered pairs together with the ordered endpoints a,c recover b. In particular the reversal of an a,b,a triple with the same removed pairs has a different added diagonal coordinate. This gives q constant types and q(q−1)² distinct proper triples. Saturation needs both new boundary types, so the two endpoint pairs are unequal-letter pairs and distinct. The triple walk must then enter and exit each equal-letter state via separate non-loop edges, and no edge can serve two distinct equal-letter states. Counting these 2q edges in addition to all proper edges gives n≥M_q+q. The proper digraph is balanced and strongly connected: from (a,b) to (c,d), use (b,c) if b≠c, or one direct edge if b=c. The added two-edge portals balance because their sources and their unmodified destinations run over the same directed cycle of unequal states. Redirecting the single exit from (0,0) balances all but the claimed start and end with the required imbalance signs. All states lie in one weak component, so an Euler trail supplies the exact-length witness. Appending any letter except the previous final letter and, if relevant, one other letter preserves distinct new endpoint changes without losing internal types. For independent uniform words the endpoint-pair event has exactly the claimed probability once the endpoint pairs are disjoint; independent interior blocks contain every proper triple and each aaa except with the stated exponentially small union-bound probability. This proves the limit and both numerical cases. Independent literal deletion and histogram checks confirm the two frozen witnesses and the internal change counts on small alphabets (python3 /workspace/replay/checks.py 4); only the classification and graph proof establish the unbounded claims.

value.rationale: The question distinguishes local ambiguity of multiplicity data from ambiguity of the strings themselves. At fixed alphabet size the sharp number of observable ordered-pair profiles is bounded independently of source length; the exact first saturation length quantifies the cost of routing through equal-letter states, and the random limit distinguishes that deterministic possibility from typical behavior. These are substantive finite-alphabet conclusions, not a global deletion-code capacity claim.
